title: S0338 (126th General Assembly): Second Amendment Privacy Act

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Draft, 2025-02-18; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/prever/338_20250218.htm (LegiScan doc 3128837))
provenance.note: Text read is the 'Draft' previous version dated 2025-02-18 (not enrolled; no passage vote in the data). Enforcement is by the Attorney General: notice, 30 business days to cure, then injunction and civil fine up to $1,000 per violation (not quoted).

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (new Section 23-31-1120): (A) Except for those records kept during the regular course of a criminal investigation and prosecution, or as otherwise required by law, no government entity or official and no agent or employee of a government entity shall knowingly keep or cause to be kept any list, record, or registry of privately owned firearms or the owners of those firearms. (B) A payment card network shall not require or incentivize the use of a merchant category code in a manner that distinguishes a firearm retailer from other retailers. (C) A covered entity shall not assign a firearm retailer a merchant category code that distinguishes the firearm retailer from other retailers.
SECTION 2 (new Section 23-31-1130): (A) The Attorney General shall investigate reasonable allegations that a person or entity, including a government entity, has violated the provisions of this article and, upon finding a violation, provide written notice to the person or entity believed to have committed the violation. (C) The Attorney General has exclusive authority to enforce the provisions of this article.
